about: Every mutant of the recorded run that the tests did not kill, by class, with a verdict and a reason. `scripts/check_mutation_survivors.py` compares a fresh run against this file and fails on a survivor it does not name, on an entry whose mutant no longer survives, and on a class without a verdict or a reason. A class called equivalent is one where the mutant computes the same thing as the original, exactly or within the rounding or the stopping tolerance the computation already admits, so no test of a reported quantity can kill it. A class called a gap is one where a test could, and none does; the entry says what such a test would have to do. `n_on_lines_the_value_records_run` counts the members that change a line tests/test_golden_values.py executes; having survived, such a mutant changes none of the values those records compare on their fixtures.

run.note: One mutant, of comparison.compare_lineage_definitions, ended the first pass with a crashed test process (mutmut reports it as segfault); run again alone, it survived. The counts above include it; the receipt of the run covers the first pass, and rerun4.out the second.

dtype-default-is-the-same.reason: `dtype=float` dropped from `np.zeros`, `np.ones`, `np.empty` or `np.full` with a float fill, whose default is already float64, or `astype(float)` rewritten as `astype(None)`, which numpy also reads as float64: the same array either way.

nan-spelling.reason: `float("nan")` rewritten as `float("NAN")`, or `float("inf")` as `float("INF")`. Python reads these strings without regard to case, so the mutant builds the same value.

warning-state.reason: an argument of `np.errstate` changed or dropped. It decides whether numpy warns about an invalid value or a division by zero, never what it computes; every such value is then masked or replaced by the code, so the result is the same.

same-maximum.reason: a change in the path of the constrained Newton iteration that computes the nonparametric maximum-likelihood distribution of the MIC readings (`mic_order._npmle`): a step length, a tolerance or an iteration budget that leaves the iteration converging to the same maximum of the concave likelihood, whose value and point are unique, to within the tolerance the iteration stops at.

same-minimum.reason: a change in the path of Wolfe's minimum-norm-point algorithm (`latent_order._minimum_norm`): the order in which ties are broken when a greedy vertex is built, the weights the corral starts from, the patience counter, a threshold of the affine step, or a point that is never read before it is computed again. Every point the algorithm visits certifies rho(x) - max(gap, GAP_TOLERANCE) as a lower end by convexity and the best is returned, so a path that still reaches a point whose gap is within the tolerance returns the same lower end within that tolerance; the minimum and the greedy vertex at any point are the same whichever tie is taken.

affine-invariant.reason: a change to the centring or the scaling of the values before the share or its standard error is computed: in `attribution._single_lineage_gain` the total sum of squares that standardises them, its divisor or the sign of the centre; in `attribution._standardised` the scale or the centre the values are put on; in `attribution._moment_se` the mean of values already centred, which is zero. The share and its standard error are the same under an increasing affine map of the values (tests/test_attribution.py checks the invariance), so the mutant computes the same interval to rounding.

guard-already-met.reason: a guard against degenerate moments whose condition the caller has already established wherever the function is reached: a positive total sum of squares (a trait constant over the scored isolates is refused before any share is computed), a positive fold ratio and a control below one (a share whose control reaches one is not estimable, and no interval is computed for it). Weakening or strengthening the guard, or joining its terms otherwise, leaves the same branch taken, so the result is the same.

symmetric-directions.reason: in `attribution._single_lineage_gain`, the sign of the second coordinate of the direction reversed. The directions scanned are SINGLE_LINEAGE_ANGLES angles spread evenly over the whole circle, a set closed under that reflection, so the same extreme points are found.

refinement-tolerance.reason: in `attribution._single_lineage_gain`, a change to the budget or the bracket of the numerical search that leaves it converging to the same extreme point: one more bisection or golden-section step, bisection limits of 31 rather than 30 on the log scale, a wider bracket around the best direction of the scan, or a slightly different shrink factor. The gain moves by less than 1e-9, below the tolerance to which tests/test_attribution.py checks it against two independent maximisations.

same-value.reason: a mutated expression that takes the same value wherever its result is read. In `attribution._single_lineage_gain`, a maximum over the scan taken over all axes where only one is non-trivial. In `latent_order._certificate`: a stratum of one isolate skipped (it holds no pair, so it adds nothing), the guard of a stratum with no isolate (every stratum holds one), a pair weight kept for lineages absent from the stratum or for tied scores (its weight is zero either way), the value given to the rows of a lineage absent from the evaluation half or from the collection (those rows are masked wherever they are read), a pair term of zero added with infinite degrees of freedom, and the degrees of freedom of no term at all (their sum is zero either way). In `latent_order.Readings`, the scan of the runs of overlapping readings started at the first reading instead of the second: that reading cannot start above its own end, so it is placed in run 0, as the zero-filled array already places it, and the reach it leaves is the one it started with. In `mic_order._npmle`, the constant subtracted from every derivative changed (1 to -1 or 2) in the slope along a direction whose entries sum to zero, where the constant contributes nothing.

search-heuristic.reason: in `latent_order._upper_search`, a change to the insertion search that proposes the attained upper share: its first start, the sort of that start, the objective of a start before its first move, the value of the top position, the tolerance of an improving move or the number of passes. The share it returns is attained by an order whatever the search finds, the branch and bound runs after it with it as incumbent, and up to EXACT_LINEAGES lineages the dynamic programme follows, so a weaker search changes no reported value on the fixtures; it could leave the attained share of more than EXACT_LINEAGES lineages lower, never invalid. In `mic_order._npmle`, the cell added to the support at each step taken as the first cell instead of the cell of the largest derivative: the iteration stops only when no derivative exceeds one by more than the tolerance, so it stops at the same maximum when it stops, and it may take more steps to get there.
search-heuristic.what_would_kill_it: an instance of more than EXACT_LINEAGES lineages on which the branch and bound does not close and the search alone, from its first start, decides the attained share; for `mic_order._npmle`, readings on which the first cell is never the steepest and the iteration budget runs out

bound-only.reason: in `latent_order._upper_certificate` and `_upper`, a change to the branch and bound that keeps its bound valid: a looser box bound, the order in which ties of the queue are taken, a node budget one larger, a node closed or opened on equality, the dynamic programme run where the bound already met the attained share. The bound stays at or above the largest share (tests/test_latent_order.py checks it against every order), and on the fixtures it closes to the same value.
bound-only.what_would_kill_it: an instance of more than EXACT_LINEAGES lineages on which the looser bound is left in the queue when the node budget runs out

power-only.reason: in `latent_order._direction`, the scores given to lineages that have no isolate in the choosing half, or the guard on how few lineages may choose. The certificate holds for every vector of scores (Theorem 2), so the limit stays valid; only its power can change, and on the fixtures no limit moves.
power-only.what_would_kill_it: a fixture whose lower limit is positive and rests on a lineage absent from one half of a split

text-not-asserted.reason: a string constant rewritten -- a key of a diagnostic block, a word of a warning, a sentinel label, the case of a status -- where no assertion reaches it. The value records compare every string of the results of the public functions, so these are strings the results do not carry on the fixtures: warnings, internal sentinels, and messages of refusals outside tests/test_refusal_messages.py.
text-not-asserted.what_would_kill_it: an assertion on the warning or the internal label, or a fixture that carries it into a result

value-not-asserted.reason: a value handed on -- a field of a returned record, an argument of a call, a fill value -- replaced by None or by another constant where the result is not read on the fixtures, or read through a path that treats the two alike (a falsy flag, a masked entry).
value-not-asserted.what_would_kill_it: a fixture that carries the value into a result the records compare

constant-not-asserted.reason: a numeric literal changed by one: an index, a gate, a tolerance, a budget, an array one longer than needed. On the fixtures the gate is not crossed, the extra element is never read, or the tolerance or budget moves no value beyond the 1e-9 the records are compared to.
constant-not-asserted.what_would_kill_it: a fixture on the gate, or an assertion on the value the constant sets

argument-dropped.reason: a keyword or positional argument removed from a call: `minlength=` of a bincount whose largest code is the last lineage on the fixtures, `stacklevel=` of a warning, `out=` of a division whose masked entries are not read, an argument equal to its default on the fixtures (`q=0.05`).
argument-dropped.what_would_kill_it: a fixture on which the argument differs from what the call does without it

boundary-comparison.reason: `<` became `<=` or the reverse. The two differ only on an input that sits exactly on the bound; no fixture sits there. Most are guards of degenerate input: a total of zero, a lineage of one, no draw left, a share of exactly zero.
boundary-comparison.what_would_kill_it: a fixture exactly on the bound

dtype-inferred-instead-of-declared.reason: a declared dtype dropped (`dtype=float`, `dtype=object`, `dtype=bool`, an integer dtype, or an `astype` target), so numpy infers one. On every fixture the inferred type is the declared one: float from float arithmetic, int64 from integer codes, bool from comparisons, object from labels.
dtype-inferred-instead-of-declared.what_would_kill_it: an input of another type at that point: integer MIC values, labels read as numbers, an empty array

branch-forced.reason: a guard rewritten to `(C) and False` or `(C) or True`, which takes the branch the fixtures never take, or both branches compute the same there.
branch-forced.what_would_kill_it: an input for which the guard takes the other branch

logical-operator.reason: `and` became `or`, or `&` became `|`, where the operands are equal on the fixtures or only one of them varies.
logical-operator.what_would_kill_it: a fixture on which the operands differ

arithmetic-operator.reason: an arithmetic operator changed where its operands make the two operators agree on the fixtures (a term that is zero, a factor that is one, a difference that no later step reads), or where the value feeds only a path no fixture takes: a count of dropped records that is zero, the gap between labelled and unlabelled records where one side is empty, an index of a chunk.
arithmetic-operator.what_would_kill_it: a fixture on which the operands differ and the value is read

control-flow.reason: `continue` became `break` or the reverse, inside a loop whose remaining iterations the fixtures make empty.
control-flow.what_would_kill_it: a fixture in which the loop has work left after the branch

accumulation-reset.reason: an augmented assignment rewritten as a plain one (`+=`, `-=`, `&=` or `|=` to `=`), where the fixtures accumulate the quantity once, or where every term before the last is zero or true, so the plain assignment leaves the same value.
accumulation-reset.what_would_kill_it: a fixture in which the quantity accumulates over more than one term that changes it

flag-flipped.reason: a boolean keyword of a pandas call flipped (`sort`, `dropna`, `as_index`, `copy`), where the fixtures give the same frame either way: keys already in order, no missing key, no duplicate to fold.
flag-flipped.what_would_kill_it: a fixture whose keys arrive out of order or carry a missing value, compared in full

unsorted.reason: a single edit the rules of this classification do not name: an index or a slice rewritten, an expression replaced by another of the same type, a method or a function exchanged for its neighbour, a comparison `==` turned into `!=` on a value the fixtures do not reach.
unsorted.what_would_kill_it: an assertion on the value the mutated expression feeds, on a fixture for which the two expressions differ

none-is-nan.reason: `np.nan` rewritten as `None` on the right of an assignment into a float array (`lo[~ok] = None`, `hi[~ok] = None` in `censored.intervals_from_mic`). numpy converts None to nan when it stores it in a float64 array, so the array the function returns is the same, entry for entry.

codec-spelling.reason: `encoding='utf-8'` rewritten as `encoding='UTF-8'` in `comparison.run_comparison` (the record and the report), and `encoding='utf-8-sig'` as `encoding='UTF-8-SIG'` in `draft._rows`. Python looks codecs up without regard to case, so the bytes written or read are the same.

disjoint-shortcut.reason: in `mic_order._stratum_scores` and `mic_order._Scorer`, the test that the readings of a stratum do not overlap replaced by a constant that fails it, so the closed form of one panel is skipped and the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimate is computed instead. On readings that do not overlap that estimate is the empirical share of every reading, the unique maximiser, and the mid-distribution scores it gives are the same as those of the closed form within the stopping tolerance of the estimate; tests/test_mic_order.py compares the two paths to 1e-12.
